surface_mechanism_description: The hydrogen-surfactant effect suppresses the segregation of substrate atoms and adatom migration, leading to the deposition of a 2D film. Hydrogen atoms prevent migration of surface adatoms and sustain 2D growth. Some H atoms are incorporated into the bulk Si, suppressing diffusion of bulk atoms and segregation of Ge atoms.
evidence: The hydrogen-surfactant effect suppresses the segregation of substrate atoms and also suppresses adatom migration resulting in the deposition of a 2D film. In SR-CVD, silicon hydride radicals and hydrogen atoms produced by the photolysis of Si2H6 gas molecules are continually supplied onto the surface. A fragment having dangling bond(s) can directly stick to the growing surface. The growing surface is continually covered by abundant H atoms which effectively prevent migration of surface adatoms and sustain 2D growth. Some of the H atoms are incorporated into the bulk Si. The H atoms suppress diffusion of bulk atoms and, consequently, segregation of Ge atoms.
